title: Old-Time Celery Storage
subtitle: 1917 USDA Wisdom
desc: Old-time celery storage inspired by USDA Farmers' Bulletin 879, Home Storage of Vegetables (1917), rewritten for today: dig celery with the roots attached, stand it upright and close together in a trench or a box in the cellar, pack moist soil around the roots while keeping the leaves dry, then cover against hard frost. A classic root cellar trick for fresh celery into winter.

title: How to Pressure Can Dry Beans
subtitle: USDA Tested Method
desc: How to safely pressure can dry beans (pinto, kidney, navy, black) following the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: soak 12–18 hours, drain, boil 30 minutes, fill hot jars with beans and cooking liquid leaving 1-inch headspace, and process pints 75 minutes or quarts 90 minutes at 10 lb (weighted gauge, 0–1,000 ft) or 11 lb (dial gauge), adjusting for altitude. Shelf-stable beans for your winter pantry.

title: How to Freeze Brussels Sprouts
subtitle: Blanch for Best Flavor
desc: How to freeze Brussels sprouts from your fall garden: trim and remove loose outer leaves, sort by size, blanch small heads 3 minutes, medium 4 and large 5, chill in ice water, drain well and pack in freezer bags with the air pressed out. Easy food preservation that keeps sprouts tasty all winter.

title: Winter Car Emergency Kit
subtitle: Be Ready on Snowy Roads
desc: Winter car emergency kit checklist: blankets and warm clothes, water and non-perishable snacks, flashlight with spare batteries, ice scraper and shovel, jumper cables, sand or kitty litter for traction, a phone charger and first aid kit. Simple winter preparedness for a self-reliant family.

title: Grow Microgreens Indoors
subtitle: Fresh Greens All Winter
desc: How to grow microgreens indoors in winter: fill a shallow tray with moist potting mix, sow radish, pea, broccoli or sunflower seeds thickly, cover until they sprout, then give bright window or grow-light light and water from below. Harvest with scissors in 7–14 days. An easy beginner garden project for fresh greens all winter.
